def solve_cvrp(instance):
    depot = instance["depot_index"]
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    customers = set(instance["customer_ids"])

    # Incumbent constructive: greedy nearest feasible with capacity exhaustion
    routes = []
    while customers:
        route = []
        load = 0
        current = depot
        while True:
            feasible = [node for node in customers if load + demands[node] <= capacity]
            if not feasible:
                break
            nxt = min(feasible, key=lambda node: (matrix[current][node], demands[node], node))
            route.append(nxt)
            customers.remove(nxt)
            load += demands[nxt]
            current = nxt
        routes.append(route)

    n = len(instance["customer_ids"])

    def route_load(r):
        s = 0
        for v in r:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

    def route_cost_full(r):
        if not r:
            return 0
        c = matrix[depot][r[0]] + matrix[r[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(r) - 1):
            c += matrix[r[i]][r[i + 1]]
        return c

    def total_cost_full(rs):
        c = 0
        for r in rs:
            c += route_cost_full(r)
        return c

    # Small edit 1: inter-route Clarke-Wright style end-to-start merges with deterministic best orientation
    # Build initial costs/loads
    loads = [route_load(r) for r in routes]
    full_costs = [route_cost_full(r) for r in routes]

    # Iteratively merge until no improving feasible merge is found
    # This keeps edits small and deterministic.
    def attempt_merge(rs, loads, full_costs, i, j, ori_i, ori_j):
        # ori_i: 0 keep, 1 reverse
        # ori_j: 0 keep, 1 reverse
        if i == j or not rs[i] or not rs[j]:
            return False
        if loads[i] + loads[j] > capacity:
            return False

        ri = rs[i]
        rj = rs[j]
        a_first, a_last = ri[0], ri[-1]
        b_first, b_last = rj[0], rj[-1]

        if ori_i == 1:
            a_first, a_last = a_last, a_first
        if ori_j == 1:
            b_first, b_last = b_last, b_first

        # connect end of i to start of j
        # remove: a_last->depot and depot->b_first, add: a_last->b_first
        delta = -matrix[a_last][depot] - matrix[depot][b_first] + matrix[a_last][b_first]
        new_full = full_costs[i] + full_costs[j] + delta
        if new_full >= full_costs[i] + full_costs[j]:
            return False  # only improving

        # apply merge
        if ori_i == 1:
            ri = ri[::-1]
        if ori_j == 1:
            rj = rj[::-1]
        rs[i] = ri + rj
        loads[i] = loads[i] + loads[j]
        full_costs[i] = new_full
        rs[j] = []
        loads[j] = 0
        full_costs[j] = 0
        return True

    # Prepare merge candidates: end-to-start savings for all active route pairs
    # Only recompute candidates a few times to keep runtime bounded.
    max_passes = 2
    for _ in range(max_passes):
        active = [idx for idx in range(len(routes)) if routes[idx]]
        if len(active) <= 1:
            break

        candidates = []
        # savings = old - new when connecting end_i -> start_j, trying both reversals by taking best delta
        for ii in range(len(active)):
            i = active[ii]
            ri = routes[i]
            a_first, a_last = ri[0], ri[-1]
            # precompute i endpoints under reversal
            i_end0, i_start0 = a_last, a_first
            i_end1, i_start1 = a_first, a_last
            for jj in range(ii + 1, len(active)):
                j = active[jj]
                rj = routes[j]
                b_first, b_last = rj[0], rj[-1]
                # j endpoints under reversal
                j_start0, j_end0 = b_first, b_last
                j_start1, j_end1 = b_last, b_first

                # Evaluate four orientations and take best (max improvement)
                best = None
                # ori_i, ori_j in {0,1} but connect end of i to start of j
                for ori_i in (0, 1):
                    i_end = i_end0 if ori_i == 0 else i_end1
                    i_start = i_start0 if ori_i == 0 else i_start1
                    for ori_j in (0, 1):
                        j_start = j_start0 if ori_j == 0 else j_start1
                        # delta in full cost

                            best = (key, delta, ori_i, ori_j)

                    improve = key[0]
                    if improve > 0 and loads[i] + loads[j] <= capacity:
                        candidates.append((improve, i, j, ori_i, ori_j))

        candidates.sort(key=lambda t: (-t[0], t[1], t[2], t[3], t[4]))

            if not routes[i] or not routes[j]:
                continue

            new_loads = []
            new_costs = []

                    new_loads.append(loads[idx])
                    new_costs.append(full_costs[idx])
            routes, loads, full_costs = new_routes, new_loads, new_costs

    # Helpers for repairs/local search
    def try_intra_2opt(r):
        # deterministic first-improvement 2-opt (segment reversal)
        m = len(r)
        if m < 4:
            return False
        # compute current internal edges cost with depot endpoints included only for comparisons locally
        # We'll evaluate delta by endpoints around i-1, i and j, j+1
        # Assume depot legs included in delta when segments touch ends.
        improved = False
        for i in range(0, m - 3):
            a = r[i - 1] if i > 0 else depot
            b = r[i]
            for j in range(i + 2, m - 1):
                c = r[j]
                d = r[j + 1] if j + 1 < m else depot
                old = matrix[a][b] + matrix[c][d]
                new = matrix[a][c] + matrix[b][d]
                if new < old:
                    r[i : j + 1] = reversed(r[i : j + 1])
                    improved = True
                    return True
        return improved

    # Small edit 2: deterministic inter-route relocate (node insertion with best position)
    def best_insertion_cost(route, pos_left, v):
        # insert v between pos_left and pos_left+1 where pos_left is index in route for left node, or -1 means before first
        if not route:
            return matrix[depot][v] + matrix[v][depot], 0  # not used
        if pos_left == -1:
            # depot->first + depot legs become depot->v + v->first
            first = route[0]
            delta = matrix[depot][v] + matrix[v][first] - matrix[depot][first]
            return delta
        if pos_left == len(route) - 1:
            last = route[-1]
            delta = matrix[last][v] + matrix[v][depot] - matrix[last][depot]
            return delta
        left = route[pos_left]
        right = route[pos_left + 1]
        delta = matrix[left][v] + matrix[v][right] - (matrix[left][right])
        return delta

    def relocate_improve(routes, loads, full_costs):
        # deterministic first-improvement: pick source route with highest load pressure, try best receiver
        # This aims to fix bottleneck structures.
        active = [k for k in range(len(routes)) if routes[k]]
        if not active:

        # order sources deterministically by decreasing route load

                else:

                    left = src[idx - 1] if idx > 0 else depot

                    new = matrix[left][right]
